stem: A 16-year-old female presents with hypomagnesemia, young-onset diabetes mellitus (MODY5), early-onset gout, and renal ultrasound showing bilateral small kidneys with cortical microcysts. Mutation in which gene is responsible for this condition?

options.text: EYA1
PAX2
HNF1B (TCF2)
GATA3

stem: A patient with branchial cleft fistulas, preauricular pits, sensorineural hearing loss, and unilateral renal agenesis is diagnosed with Branchio-Oto-Renal (BOR) Syndrome. Which gene mutation is most frequently associated with this autosomal dominant disorder?

options.text: WT1
PKD1
NPHS2
EYA1

stem: A newborn delivered at 34 weeks displays pulmonary hypoplasia, compressed facies (low-set ears, flattened nose), and limb positional deformities. Autopsy reveals bilateral renal agenesis. What is the primary pathogenetic cascade leading to these extrarenal deformities?

options.text: In utero Oligohydramnios leading to mechanical uterine compression of the fetus
Direct systemic toxic effect of unexcreted uremic toxins
Excess maternal progesterone stimulation during organogenesis
Congenital vascular malformation of the umbilical arteries

stem: Antenatal ultrasound detects a non-functioning unilateral kidney composed of multiple large non-communicating cysts separated by dysplastic stroma, with complete absence of normal renal parenchyma. What is the recommended long-term management strategy for this Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney (MCDK)?

options.text: Immediate neonatal surgical nephrectomy to prevent malignant transformation
Conservative serial ultrasound observation for involution and screening the contralateral kidney for anomalies
Prophylactic bilateral ureteral reimplantation
High-dose steroid pulse therapy to halt cyst expansion

stem: Which of the following statements regarding Ectopic Kidney and Crossed Fused Ectopia is CORRECT?

options.text: Pelvic kidneys typically have an elongated normal ureter that becomes kinked
Horseshoe kidney is completely free of any increased risk for Nephrolithiasis or UPJO
Renal rotation during embryonic ascent normally causes the renal pelvis to face posteriorly
In Crossed Fused Ectopia, the crossed ectopic kidney lies on the opposite side of its ureteral insertion into the bladder
